title: Nonzero embedding count and the separability equality test
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields [def-weil-field] such that $L$ is a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space of dimension $d$. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field equipped with an embedding $K\hookrightarrow\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Put $t=|\operatorname{Hom}_{K\text{-alg}}(L,\Omega)|$, where these are field homomorphisms whose restriction to $K$ is the specified embedding. Then this set is finite and nonempty, so $t\ge1$, and $t=d$ if and only if $L/K$ is separable: the minimal polynomial over $K$ of every element of $L$ has distinct roots in an algebraic closure. Algebraicity of $\Omega/K$ is not assumed.

mathlib_match.how: One declaration per clause after the counting identification: Field.finSepDegree_eq_of_isAlgClosed at lines 237–238 identifies Nat.card (L →ₐ[K] Ω) with Field.finSepDegree K L; finite-dimensional implies Algebra.IsAlgebraic. Field.instNeZeroFinSepDegree at lines 145–146 makes this natural count nonzero, hence positive and the embedding set finite and nonempty (Nat.card is zero on infinite types). Field.finSepDegree_eq_finrank_iff at lines 774–775 gives the equality iff Algebra.IsSeparable K L. These declarations and their hypotheses were read at lines 127–146, 229–238 and 771–786. Algebra.IsSeparable is the usual separability of all minimal polynomials; fields make algebra homomorphisms injective. No normality, perfection or algebraicity of the target is required.
